Dying Light 2 is one of my favorite games. An absolute masterpiece. The characters are memorable, and the world looks awesome. Villedor’s environment offers so much variety that exploring never feels dull. The parkour is one of the best parts of Dying Light 2. The best parkour mechanics in the entire Dying Light series is definitely in Dying Light 2. That’s because the variety of spots and moves is unbelievable. You can mix up different parkour styles and moves almost anywhere you go. Moving through the city feels very smooth and satisfying.

I also enjoyed the Tower Raid experience. it added variety to the gameplay. Personally, I find the story stronger than the first game, especially because of the characters and world design. The many activities, locations, enemies, and ways to approach situations keep every playthrough fresh. After 100 hours and five playthroughs, I am still coming back for more.

Gave this game way more time than it deserved and will likely be one of the only games I stopped playing for the sole reason of not enjoying it. I don't need to even get into all the reasons why, seeing as plenty of other reviews already do. 

Even if the game mechanically felt like the first, each story mission just feels like "go do this for me and maybe we'll talk" to "oh you did what I asked? well I'm still not giving you what you want" to "make a "game changing" choice right now" which doesn't actually feel like it ever has any real impact at all. 

And before this gets misconstrued as wanting instant gratification, yes and no. Usually playing games, it's to feel as though we have accomplished something or are at least are on our way to accomplishing something with every task we're given. This game fails to do that, and if anything makes every single mission feel as though its a painstakingly boring chore, rather actually progressing for the reason of moving the plot along.

Genuinely one of the dumbest games I've played in a long time. Mechanically, it's fun. The parkour makes you feel cool and getting around the city can be a blast. That's one of the only good things I can say about this trash pile.

All of the characters are unlikeable besides Frank and that's a low bar to be set; the combat is laughably easy even on the highest difficulty; the story continuously makes no sense (from the standpoint of how you'd react in these situations) and your choices mean little; Aiden is a nothingburger character who will agree to do anything, even walk into obvious traps; most lootables are crafting reagents that you'll be overflowing with by the endgame or valuables to simply sell for money you'll hardly be compelled to use outside of upgrading weapon enhancements that you'll attach to a select set of weapons that you'll never stray from. 

Everything about this game is dumb. I was enjoying my first 10 hours as a returning DL1 player. Then the dumb just hit like a waterfall and I couldn't shake it. At a certain point, I just needed to finish the game so my time spent didn't feel wasted but ultimately I regret the 50-some hours I put into this game.

Just go back and play Dying Light 1. Don't waste your money on this garbage.

Played this mostly for its co-op together with a friend and man... does it open my eyes on how basic forgettable features helps enrich the experience. Dying Light 2 misses so much of this making the co-op experience feel incredibly hollow. Simple things like hearing the grunts from other players when they fight or parkour, flashlights being synchronized between clients, all actions being properly animated in 3rd person, etc. Player creativity could have made having the above hilariously entertaining and enriching, but  I guess that's too much to ask for. 

What the hell happened during the development cycle of this game? The story feels like a weird frankenstein where it feels like a bunch of content is disjointed or cut prior to release and it's overall an incredibly buggy experience to an excessive degree. We can all agree that the occasional bug can make for hilarious moments, but the sheer amount you run into in this game makes me shake my head.

Because the game lacks a lot of the enriching features it ends up feeling especially grind-y and repetitive. I really wish to complete it prior to playing Dying Light The Beast just to not miss out on picking up on references, but it's been such a slog that I just might end up doing that.

I [b]LOVED[/b] and still [b]LOVE[/b] Dying Light, and when a sequal was annouced I was [b]THRILLED, EXCITED[/b] and as happy as a child is on Christmas Day morning but I was hesitant. I did pre-order the first game when it first came around but I didn't with Dying Light 2. I held off for a really long time because of the disaster that followed the launch of the game. I just couldn't take myself to be a part of it. I just observed everything, waited and had my hopes up that Techland would listen to the community and fans of the IP and start to change things.

Dying Light 2 was so criticized for the longest time and had alot of problems, but when they annonunced the new game [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/3008130/Dying_Light_The_Beast/]Dying Light: The Beast[/url] as being included FOR FREE with the previously available Ultimate Edition of Dying Light 2 I finally bought this game back in 2024 to not miss such a great deal and now I'm finally playing through this game and I'm having a really great time. 

Dying Light 2 has gone through a major glow up, many issues previously present has been addressed and many things that caused concern is no longer present in the game. Stealth has been fixed, nights have been fixed, guns has been added, loadouts and gear transmogs, parkour has been fixed, intro was changed twice, NG+ added and nightmare difficulty was added and the previous prologue has been removed? Removed? Why? HELLO?! WHAT IS HAPPENING? No one knows for sure but something about the narrative for the new game. Really bad change in my opinion. 
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3812166842
Either way I'm having a blast playing the game, I don't get the negative spin that people have over the story, I like the story alot and the characters are not forgettable, quite the opposite and so far I like the antagonist Waltz, atleast where I am so far in the story being 100+ hours into the game. I've just made it into the Central Loop and It's great. I have mostly been playing around without doing the main questline. 

I do 100% recommend this game, especially with all the changes that has happened since launch. The game is in a good enough state that I'm having an amazing time playing. Combat feels great, weapons feel responsive and powerful, zombies feel scary, humans feels dangerous, world feels alive, music and atmosphere in the game is lovely. the gore is AO-rated for sure. 
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3814661463
One major issue that is recurring is the constant crashing of the game. Game freezes suddenly and then crashes without warning whenever. The first three times I just booted the game and continued where I was so suddenly abrupted but it's starting to get really annoying, even though starting the game doesn't take long, It's still frustrating and annoying as hell.

Game is as of now a B+ tier and it's really great, pick it up and give it a try. Doubt you will be disappointed if you liked the first game. It's different and requires some adjusting but once you get the flow of the show, you really get a great show.

Made by the same people who do Dead Island; if you've played that then the system is familiar (or vice versa).

Great parkour system, perfect game for if you love committing mass genocide through unnecessarily gory methods (that can be made even worse using mods, such as tearing off someone's jaw whilst still alive), sadly a story that's decent first time around but is then unbearable on further runs due to truth reveals that leave you spending every NPC discussion disagreeing with your screen and calling them idiots.

Even after the story is done there's still several different side missions, multiple Easter Eggs (including a pixelated DOOM event), countless community-made maps, a tower raid mode that can be repeated endlessly, no real end to personal progress (even after you're fully upgraded you then have "legend" levels that allow even more upgrades), and of course an endless amount of targets to satisfy your bloodlust.

And if you don't want to slaughter people with melee weapons you can use the recently added guns. 
Don't complain that you can't use them immediately, as the game wasn't built for them.
